correctness.rationale: The greedy binary arch index is the matching number of unequal-adjacency path edges. Removing edge j of a transition chain of length ell reduces its ceiling(ell/2) matching number exactly when ell and j are odd. This yields the exact number of bad cuts and stability condition. Even transition chains tile uniquely into pairs, except the all-ones even circle with two pairings; trace([[1,1],[u,0]]^n) with a correction and two binary integrations proves the full coefficient formula. The self-contained verifier separately enumerated all 524286 binary words through n=18 and full subsequence sets through n=9, with exact integer agreement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General-alphabet circular index and repetition results do not enumerate all binary words for which every rotation simultaneously attains the circular maximum. The matching approach uses a binary-specific unequal-adjacency simplification absent from these general statements.

originality.rationale: Inspected foundational circular-universality results give the one-arch bound and algorithms, but not a criterion for equality at every cyclic cut or the corresponding all-indexed-word Lucas enumeration. Classical Lucas counts for matchings of cycles do not identify which original binary words have cut-independent subsequence universality. A separate earlier cyclic-maximum count likewise does not determine the minimum without the essential-edge classification. Equivalent statements in unindexed work are a residual risk.

value.rationale: Subsequence universality of a circular string can depend on where reading begins. The result completely classifies cut-robust binary words, gives an exact number of harmful cut positions for every word, and the full length-and-index joint enumeration; the exponentially vanishing robust fraction quantifies a natural origin-ambiguity issue. This goes beyond a tiny finite parameter gain or a bare known-sequence recomputation.
